author: Goodnighht
body:
Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?
Yes, I was a Moderator on Avicus.
What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?
My biggest weakness is that sometimes I can be slow with punishments, but I don't think it effects my moderating very much because the job still gets done.
My biggest strength is that I can be online a lot. I haven't been more recently, but I don't have a reason to be active anymore.
How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
I can be active. I don't have a lot of homework so I can, most of the time, just come home from school and come online. 
What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
A leader needs to be able to understand what other people need to learn, as well as be able to learn themselves. A leader also needs to be able to speak up for what they think is right. That is very important because if a leader always says "Yes, that's correct." or "Yes, I agree.", even when they don't agree then nothing is being done about things that might be wrong or need to be fixed.
I like to think that I can be a leader when I need to be, although I still have a lot to learn I feel like when I do learn something I can normally teach it fairly well. 
What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
I have previous experience being a Moderator as well as being able to be online a lot. I am also able to handle keeping a situation mature and not let it get out of hand. 
What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?
You should be able to respond with confidence with most questions they ask you, and if you don't know the answer you should be willing to admit that you don't know. There should also be a level of trust between you and the community, because without a trust that you're not going to give them a stupid punishment it's not likely that anyone will come to you, or the staff team for help if they need it.

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 
On weekdays I can usually be reachable 7-9 hours. On weekends I'm normally reachable around 9-12 hours a day but I will be a lot less likely to respond because most of the time I am playing other games with friends.

CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?
Keep freezing the person and keep track of all of the accounts by leaving the name in a Slack/Discord chat until someone can get online to help you.

Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?
First I would ask them to stop and if they don't then I would record and report it to a Senior Staff member.

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realise that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?
You have to appeal the ban, because you have no evidence. After that you just wait for them to come back online and hack again. If they come back and aren't hacking then the ban/appeal did the job and there's nothing to worry about.
You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?
Tell a Senior Staff member and let them handle it. There's nothing I can do.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?
I would make it clear I don't agree and try to find out more about what happened. I don't want to jump to any conclusions without all the information.

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?
I can't really say it means a lot, but it gives me a reason to be online and connect with everyone more. I also feel like it's the best way for me to help the community.

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?
I love Avicus, I've been around four years now, and I still remember the first Walls map. I still remember my favorite kit from then and my routes on all the old maps. Since I've joined I've made a ton of friends here. A lot of them are still around but some sadly have left. Avicus has been my place to escape from IRL things, and it has been the place that I come to have fun. Over the past four years Avicus has become one of my favorite things to invest my time into, whether it's talking with people or helping in some way. 

Do you speak any other languages than English?
Um... Hola?
(No, I do not.)
Do you have anything else to add to your application?
No.
